and the other two possible morphism spaces are both zero. The map of complexes induced by the non-zero morphism in
\hom_{\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}}(\mathrm{B}_{1}\langle-1\rangle,\mathrm{B}_{01})
is null-homotopic, with the homotopy being induced by the identity on
\mathrm{B}_{1}\langle-1\rangle
. The map of complexes induced by the non-zero morphism in
\hom_{\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}}(\mathrm{B}_{101}\langle-1\rangle,\mathrm{B}_{10})
is not null-homotopic,
because Soergel’s hom formula implies that
\hom_{\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}}(\mathrm{B}_{101}\langle-1\rangle,\mathrm{B}_{0}\langle-1\rangle)=\hom_{\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}}(\mathrm{B}_{101}\langle-1\rangle,\mathrm{B}_{1}\langle-1\rangle)=0
, so there are no morphisms which could constitute a homotopy.

Note that this implies that
\mathrm{hom}_{\mathrm{Y}}(\mathrm{B}_{01}\mathrm{Y},\mathrm{B}_{01}\mathrm{Y})
contains a non-zero morphism which is not
a multiple of an idempotent.

Theorem 5.22
.

The following holds in
\mathbf{U}
.

(1)

We have

\mathrm{B}_{\rho}\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,0}}\mathrm{Y}\cong\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,1}}\mathrm{B}_{\rho}\mathrm{Y}\cong\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}\langle-1\rangle,\quad\forall\,k\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}.

(2)

We have

\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,0}}\mathrm{Y}\cong\mathrm{B}_{\rho}\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}\langle-1\rangle,\quad\forall\,k\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}.

(3)

The indecomposables

\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}\langle s\rangle,\;\mathrm{B}_{\rho}\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{m}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}\langle t\rangle,\quad k,m\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0};s,t\in\mathbb{Z}

are pairwise non-isomorphic.

Proof.

(a)

The isomorphism
\mathrm{B}_{1}\mathrm{T}_{1}\cong\mathrm{B}_{1}\langle-1\rangle
in
K^{b}(\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2})
and the isomorphism
\mathrm{B}_{\rho}\mathrm{Y}\cong\mathrm{T}_{1}\mathrm{Y}
in
\mathbf{U}

imply that

\mathrm{B}_{\rho}\mathrm{B}_{0}\mathrm{Y}\cong\mathrm{B}_{1}\mathrm{B}_{\rho}\mathrm{Y}\cong\mathrm{B}_{1}\mathrm{T}_{1}\mathrm{Y}\cong\mathrm{B}_{1}\mathrm{Y}\langle-1\rangle\;\,\text{in}\;\,\mathbf{U}.

The general result, as stated in the theorem, follows by induction and uniqueness of decomposition into indecomposables in
\mathbf{U}
, because

\mathrm{B}_{0}\mathrm{B}_{1}\cong\mathrm{B}_{01}\quad\text{and}\quad\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k-1}_{\,0}}\mathrm{B}_{1}\cong\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,1}}\oplus\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k-2}_{\,1}}\;\,\text{in}\;\,\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2},

for all
k\in\mathbb{Z}_{>2}
.

(b)

The isomorphism in this case can be obtained from the one in the previous case by tensoring with
\mathrm{B}_{\rho}
on the left and using that

\mathrm{B}_{\rho}^{2}
acts as the identity on
\mathbf{U}
.

(c)

There are three different cases: we have to show that

(a)

\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}\langle s\rangle\not\cong\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{m}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}\langle t\rangle
, for
k,m\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}
with
k\neq m
and
s,t\in\mathbb{Z}
;

(b)

\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}\langle s\rangle\not\cong\mathrm{B}_{\rho}\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{m}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}\langle t\rangle
, for
k,m\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}
and
s,t\in\mathbb{Z}
;

(c)

\mathrm{B}_{\rho}\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}\langle s\rangle\not\cong\mathrm{B}_{\rho}\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{m}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}\langle t\rangle
, for
k,m\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}
with
k\neq m
and
s,t\in\mathbb{Z}
.

The first case implies the third one, because

\mathrm{hom}_{\mathrm{Y}}(\mathrm{B}_{\rho}\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{m}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}\langle t\rangle,\mathrm{B}_{\rho}\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y})\cong\mathrm{hom}_{\mathrm{Y}}(\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{m}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}\langle t\rangle,\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y})

by adjunction, so it suffices to prove the first two cases.

i) Suppose that there is an isomorphism in
\mathbf{U}

f\colon\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}\langle t\rangle\to\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{m}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}

for some
k,m\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}
with
k\neq m
and some
t\in\mathbb{Z}
, which we may assume to be non-negative without loss of generality. As before,

f
is determined by its non-zero components in
K^{b}(\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2})

f^{r,s}\colon\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,1}}\langle t\rangle\to\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{m}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}^{r,s}

for a finite number of integers
r,s
. By
[
MaTh
, Theorem 2.5]
and
Proposition 5.19
, this implies that
r+s=0
and
r\leq 0
. Since
t\geq 0
and
k\neq m
, both by assumption,
Soergel’s hom formula (
49
) implies that
f^{-s,s}=0
if
s=0
. Thus, we must have
s>0
for all non-zero
f^{-s,s}
. Recall that

\mathrm{Y}^{-s,s}\simeq(\mathrm{T}_{1}^{-1}\mathrm{T}_{0}^{-1})^{s}
and that the minimal complex
[(\mathrm{T}_{1}^{-1}\mathrm{T}_{0}^{-1})^{s}]^{\mathrm{min}}
is given by

\cdots\xlongrightarrow{}\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{s-1}_{\,0}}\langle-1\rangle\oplus\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{s-1}_{\,1}}\langle-1\rangle\xlongrightarrow{\mathrm{d}^{-1}}\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{s}_{\,0}}.

By adjunction, we also have

\mathrm{hom}_{K^{b}(\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2})}(\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,1}}\langle t\rangle,\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{m}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}^{-s,s})\cong\mathrm{hom}_{K^{b}(\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2})}(\mathrm{B}_{{}_{1}\widehat{m}}\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,1}}\langle t\rangle,\mathrm{Y}^{-s,s}),

and (
123
) and
3.3
imply that the indecomposables in the decomposition of
\mathrm{B}_{{}_{1}\widehat{m}}\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,1}}\langle t\rangle
are of the form

\mathrm{B}_{{}_{1}\widehat{n}_{\,1}}\langle t^{\prime}\rangle
, for certain integers
n\geq|k-m|
and certain
t^{\prime}\in\{t-1,t,t+1\}
. Since
k\neq m
, we must have
n>0
. Therefore,
Soergel’s hom formula (
49
) implies that

\mathrm{hom}_{\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}}(\mathrm{B}_{{}_{1}\widehat{n}_{\,1}}\langle t^{\prime}\rangle,\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{s}_{\,0}})=0

for all integers
n,s>0
and
t^{\prime}\geq 0
. Since
t^{\prime}<0
can only hold if
t\leq 0
, our initial assumption that
t\geq 0
implies that we must have
t=0
and
t^{\prime}=-1
. However, this leads to a contradiction.
Since
f^{-s,s}
is zero unless
s>0
, the inverse of
f
must have a non-zero component
(f^{-1})^{s,-s}\colon\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{m}_{\,1}}\to\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}^{s,-s}
for some
s>0
, which is
impossible according to
Proposition 5.19
. This completes the proof that the
\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}\langle t\rangle

are all pairwise non-isomorphic.

ii) It suffices to show that
\mathrm{B}_{\rho}\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}\not\cong\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{m}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}\langle t\rangle
, for any
k,m\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}
and any
t\in\mathbb{Z}
. First assume that
k=m=0
and suppose, on the contrary, that there is an isomorphism

f\colon\mathrm{B}_{\rho}\mathrm{Y}\to\mathrm{Y}\langle t\rangle

for some
t\in\mathbb{Z}
. By tensoring on the left with
\mathrm{B}_{\rho}
and using the fact that
\mathrm{B}_{\rho}^{2}
acts as the identity, we see that

t
has to be zero. Further,
f
is determined by its non-zero components
f^{r,s}\colon\mathrm{B}_{\rho}\to\mathrm{Y}^{r,s}
.
By
[
MaTh
, Theorem 2.5]
, such a component can only be non-zero if
r+s=1
, so assume this and assume also that
r\geq 1
. Then

\mathrm{Y}^{r,s}\simeq\mathrm{B}_{\rho}\mathrm{T}_{\widehat{2r-1}_{\,1}}
.
By adjunction, we have

(147)

\mathrm{hom}_{K^{b}(\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2})}(\mathrm{B}_{\rho},\mathrm{B}_{\rho}\mathrm{T}_{\widehat{2r-1}_{\,1}})\cong\mathrm{hom}_{K^{b}(\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2})}(R,\mathrm{T}_{\widehat{2r-1}_{\,1}}).

The minimal complex
[\mathrm{T}_{\widehat{2r-1}_{\,1}}]^{\min}
is given by
\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{2r-1}_{\,1}}
in homological degree zero, so Soergel’s hom
formula in (
49
) implies that the second morphism space in (
147
) is zero because
2r-1>0
. The case
when
r<1
can be proved similarly. This implies that
f^{r,s}=0
for all
r,s\in\mathbb{Z}
, which proves that
\mathrm{B}_{\rho}\mathrm{Y}
can not
be isomorphic to
\mathrm{Y}\langle t\rangle
for any
t\in\mathbb{Z}
.

Now assume that
k>0
. Item b) implies that the proof is complete if we can show that
\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,0}}\mathrm{Y}
and
\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{m}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}\langle t\rangle
are not isomorphic for any
m\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}
and any
t\in\mathbb{Z}
. Note that the case when
m>0
reduces to the case when
k>0
by tensoring both complexes on the left with
\mathrm{B}_{\rho}
and using that
\mathrm{B}_{\rho}^{2}
acts as the identity, so we can indeed assume
that
k>0
without loss of generality. Now, suppose in that case that there exists an isomorphism

(148)

f\colon\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,0}}\mathrm{Y}\langle t\rangle\to\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{m}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}

in
\mathbf{U}
, for some
k,m\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}
and
t\in\mathbb{Z}
.

We will first show that
t=1
must hold. Then we will show that
\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,0}}\langle 1\rangle
must be a direct summand of
\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{m}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}^{-s,s}
for some
s>0
.
Finally, we will show that that is impossible. To arrive at that contradiction, we will first show that there is only a monomorphism
\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,0}}\langle 1\rangle\to\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{m}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}^{-s,s}
for
k=1
, but that there is no epimorphism
\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{m}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}^{-s,s}\to\mathrm{B}_{0}\langle 1\rangle
. To prove that
k=1
must hold, we use
localization
, which we briefly recall in the beginning of the relevant paragraph.

Note that

\displaystyle\mathrm{hom}(\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,0}}\mathrm{Y}\langle t\rangle,\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{m}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y})

\displaystyle\cong

\displaystyle\mathrm{hom}(\mathrm{B}_{\rho}\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,0}}\mathrm{Y}\langle t\rangle,\mathrm{B}_{\rho}\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{m}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y})

\displaystyle\cong

\displaystyle\mathrm{hom}(\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}\langle t-1\rangle,\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{m}_{\,0}}\mathrm{Y}\langle 1\rangle)

\displaystyle\cong

\displaystyle\mathrm{hom}(\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y},\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{m}_{\,0}}\mathrm{Y}\langle 2-t\rangle).

Hence, the inverse of
f
induces an isomorphism
\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{m}_{\,0}}\mathrm{Y}\langle 2-t\rangle\to\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}
in
\mathbf{U}
. Since
t\leq 1
if and only if
2-t\geq 1
, we can assume that

t\geq 1
in (
148
) without loss of generality. Thus, let
t\geq 1
. As before, the isomorphism
f
is determined by its components

f^{r,s}\colon\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,0}}\langle t\rangle\to\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{m}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}^{r,s}.

By
[
MaTh
, Theorem 2.5]
and
Proposition 5.19
, we have
f^{r,s}=0
unless
r+s=0
and
r\leq 0
. Soergel’s hom formula in (
49
) implies that
f^{0,0}=0
, thus
all non-zero components
f^{r,-r}
satisfy
r<0
(which is equivalent to saying that
f^{-s,s}\neq 0
can only hold if
s>0
, of course).

Now, suppose that
s=-r>0
. We claim that
t=1
must hold. Note that
\mathrm{Y}^{-s,s}\simeq(\mathrm{T}_{1}^{-1}\mathrm{T}_{0}^{-1})^{s}
and the
0
-cochain object of

[(\mathrm{T}_{1}^{-1}\mathrm{T}_{0}^{-1})^{s}]^{\min}
is
\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{2s}_{\,0}}
. By adjunction, we have

\mathrm{hom}_{K^{b}(\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2})}(\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,0}}\langle t\rangle,\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{m}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}^{-s,s})\cong\mathrm{hom}_{K^{b}(\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2})}(\mathrm{B}_{{}_{1}\widehat{m}}\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,0}}\langle t\rangle,\mathrm{Y}^{-s,s}),

and the indecomposables in the decomposition of
\mathrm{B}_{{}_{1}\widehat{m}}\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,0}}\langle t\rangle
are all of the form

\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{n}_{\,0}}\langle t^{\prime}\rangle
for certain
n\geq|k-m|
and
t^{\prime}\in\{t-1,t,t+1\}
. Soergel’s hom formula in (
49
) implies that

\mathrm{hom}_{\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}}(\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{n}_{\,0}}\langle t^{\prime}\rangle,\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{2s}_{\,0}})

is zero for all
t^{\prime}>0
(and any
n\geq 0
) and is one-dimensional for
t^{\prime}=0
(in which case
n=2s
). This shows that
f^{-s,s}\neq 0
implies that
t^{\prime}=0
, which can only hold if
t=1
since

t\geq 1
by assumption. This completes the proof of the claim.

Now suppose that
g=f^{-1}
. Then there must be an integer
s>0
such that the following
composite is non-zero:

\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,0}}\langle 1\rangle\xrightarrow{f^{-s,s}}\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{m}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}^{-s,s}\xrightarrow{g^{s,-s}\circ\,\mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{Y}^{-s,s}}}\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,0}}\langle 1\rangle\mathrm{Y}^{s,-s}\mathrm{Y}^{-s,s}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,0}}\langle 1\rangle\circ\mu}}\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,0}}\langle 1\rangle,

where we have used the canonical isomorphism
\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,0}}\mathrm{Y}^{0,0}\langle 1\rangle\cong\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,0}}\langle 1\rangle
for the final codomain. Soergel’s hom formula in
(
49
) implies that that composite is a non-zero multiple of the
identity, hence
\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,0}}\langle 1\rangle
is a direct summand of

\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{m}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}^{-s,s}
. However, that is impossible, as we will show below.

First identify
\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
with the algebraic category of Soergel bimodules over
R
(the polynomial ring generated by the dumbbells). Let
Q
be the field of fractions of
R
and recall the
localization functor

\mathrm{Loc}\colon\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}\to\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2,Q}
, defined by
forgetting the grading of Soergel bimodules and tensoring them on the right with
Q
(over
R
), see
[
EMTW
, Section 5.4]
.
By
[
EMTW
, Lemma 5.20]
, this is a monoidal functor. For any
u\in\widehat{\mathfrak{S}}_{2}
, let
Q_{u}
be the
standard

Q
-
Q
-bimodule,
which is the one-dimensional
Q
-vector space with left and right
Q
-actions defined by

x\cdot q\cdot y:=xqu(y),

for
q,x,y\in Q
. For any
u,v\in\widehat{\mathfrak{S}}_{2}
, we have

Q_{u}Q_{v}\cong Q_{uv}
, see e.g.
[
EMTW
, (5.5)]
, and the morphism spaces between the standard
Q
-
Q
-bimodules are very easy
to describe (as follows from e.g.
[
EMTW
, Lemma 5.2]
):

\mathrm{hom}_{Q\text{-}Q-\mathrm{bimod}}(Q_{u},Q_{v})\cong\begin{cases}Q,&\mathrm{if}\;u=v;\\
0,&\mathrm{else}.\end{cases}

As indicated in the commutative diagram
[
EMTW
, (5.25)]
and proved in
[
EMTW
, Theorem 18.22]
, for every
w\in\widehat{\mathfrak{S}}_{2}
, we have

B_{w}\otimes_{R}Q\cong\bigoplus_{u\preceq w}Q_{u},

because in affine type
A_{1}
we have
p_{u,w}(1)=1
for all
u\preceq w
and zero else (where
p_{u,w}
is the Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial for
u,w\in\widehat{\mathfrak{S}}_{2}
). Concretely, this means that

\mathrm{Loc}\left(B_{\widehat{n}_{\,i}}\right)\cong Q_{\widehat{n}_{\,i}}\oplus\bigoplus_{0<l<n}\left(Q_{\widehat{l}_{\,0}}\oplus Q_{\widehat{l}_{\,1}}\right)\oplus Q,

for any
n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}
and
i\in\{0,1\}
(note that
Q_{\widehat{0}_{\,i}}=Q
). Localization can also be applied to Rouquier complexes and
[
EMTW
, Lemma 5.21]
implies that, for every
w\in\widehat{\mathfrak{S}}_{2}
, we have

\mathrm{Loc}(\mathrm{T}_{w})\simeq Q_{w}\quad\text{and}\quad\mathrm{Loc}(\mathrm{T}^{-1}_{w})\simeq Q_{w^{-1}}.

The results in the previous paragraph imply that
\mathrm{Loc}(\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,0}})
must be a
direct summand of
\mathrm{Loc}\left(\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{m}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}^{-s,s}\right)
, which imposes conditions on
k
,
m
and
s
.
On the one hand, we get

\mathrm{Loc}(\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,0}})\cong Q_{\widehat{k}_{\,0}}\oplus\bigoplus_{0<l<k}\left(Q_{\widehat{l}_{\,0}}\oplus Q_{\widehat{l}_{\,1}}\right)\oplus Q

and, on the other hand, we get

\displaystyle\mathrm{Loc}\left(\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{m}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}^{-s,s}\right)\cong

\displaystyle\left(Q_{\widehat{m}_{\,1}}\oplus\bigoplus_{0<n<m}\left(Q_{\widehat{n}_{\,0}}\oplus Q_{\widehat{n}_{\,1}}\right)\oplus Q\right)Q_{{}_{1}\widehat{2s}_{\,0}}\cong

\displaystyle Q_{\widehat{|m-2s|}_{\,0}}\oplus\bigoplus_{0<n<m}\left(Q_{\widehat{n+2s}_{\,0}}\oplus Q_{\widehat{|n-2s|}_{\,0}}\right)\oplus Q_{{}_{1}\widehat{2s}_{\,0}}.

By the Krull-Schmidt property of
\mathrm{add}(\bigoplus_{w\in\widehat{\mathfrak{S}}_{2}}Q_{w})
, where the additive closure is taken in the category of all
Q
-
Q
-bimodules, we see that

\mathrm{Loc}(\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,0}})
can only be a direct summand of

\mathrm{Loc}\left(\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{m}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}^{-s,s}\right)
if
k=1
and
m\geq 2s
.

Thus we have an embedding
f^{-s,s}\colon\mathrm{B}_{0}\langle 1\rangle\to\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{m}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}^{-s,s}
in
K^{b}(\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2})
, with
m\geq 2s
. By adjunction, this implies that there is a non-zero morphism
\mathrm{B}_{{}_{1}\widehat{m}}\mathrm{B}_{0}\langle 1\rangle\to\mathrm{Y}^{-s,s}
. Since
[\mathrm{Y}^{-s,s}]^{\min}
is given by

\mathrm{B}_{{}_{1}\widehat{2s}_{\,0}}
in homological degree zero, such a non-zero morphism can only exist if
m=2s
, thanks to
3.3
and equations (
49
) and (
123
). In particular, we have

\mathrm{B}_{{}_{0}\widehat{2s}_{\,1}}\mathrm{B}_{{}_{1}\widehat{2s}_{\,0}}\cong\left(\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{4s-1}_{\,0}}\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathrm{B}_{0}\right)^{q+q^{-1}},

so the embedding
f^{-s,s}\colon\mathrm{B}_{0}\langle 1\rangle\to\mathrm{B}_{{}_{0}\widehat{2s}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}^{-s,s}
is induced by the identity on
\mathrm{B}_{0}\langle 1\rangle
. However, we claim that that embedding does not split. Recall that
[\mathrm{Y}^{-s,s}]^{\min}\cong[(\mathrm{T}_{1}^{-1}\mathrm{T}_{0}^{-1})^{s}]^{\mathrm{min}}
is given by

\cdots\xlongrightarrow{}\mathrm{B}_{{}_{0}\widehat{2s-1}_{\,0}}\langle-1\rangle\oplus\mathrm{B}_{{}_{1}\widehat{2s-1}_{\,1}}\langle-1\rangle\xlongrightarrow{\mathrm{d}^{-1}}\underline{\mathrm{B}_{{}_{1}\widehat{2s}_{\,0}}}

where

\mathrm{d}^{-1}=(\mathrm{d}^{-1}_{\mathrm{L}},\mathrm{d}^{-1}_{\mathrm{R}})=\left(\lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.5pt\hbox{\kern 26.00708pt\hbox{{\hbox{\kern-26.00708pt\raise 0.14226pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise-33.45007pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\hbox to52.01pt{\vbox to66.9pt{\pgfpicture\makeatletter\hbox{\hskip 26.00708pt\lower-33.45007pt\hbox to0.0pt{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin} \lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke} \lxSVG@begingroup@{fill} \lxSVG@setlinewidth{\the\pgflinewidth}\lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke-width} \lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\nullfont\hbox to0.0pt{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin} {{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}}{{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}}\lxSVG@setlinewidth{\the\pgflinewidth}\lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke-width} \lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{

Tensoring this complex on the left with
\mathrm{B}_{{}_{0}\widehat{2s}_{\,1}}
(over
R
) yields a complex containing the morphism

\mathrm{B}_{{}_{0}\widehat{2s}_{\,1}}\mathrm{B}_{{}_{1}\widehat{2s-1}_{\,1}}\langle-1\rangle\xlongrightarrow{\mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{B}_{{}_{0}\widehat{2s}_{\,1}}}\circ\,\mathrm{d}^{-1}_{\mathrm{R}}}\underline{\mathrm{B}_{{}_{0}\widehat{2s}_{\,1}}\mathrm{B}_{{}_{1}\widehat{2s}_{\,0}}}

When we compose this morphism with the projection of
\mathrm{B}_{{}_{0}\widehat{2s}_{\,1}}\mathrm{B}_{{}_{1}\widehat{2s}_{\,0}}
onto
\mathrm{B}_{0}\langle 1\rangle
, we get a non-zero multiple of

0
1
1
0
\cdots
\mathrm{JW}_{(0,\ldots,1)}
1
0
1
\cdots
\mathrm{JW}_{(1,\ldots,0)}
0

It is easy to see that the latter diagram is non-zero. For example, attaching a dot to the top

0
-strand and cups to the
2s
bottom left strands, and using adjunction to straighten the resulting diagram, yields

1
0
1
\cdots
1
0
0
1
\cdots
\mathrm{JW}_{(1,\ldots,0)}

which is non-zero, as we know. This implies that the projection of
\mathrm{B}_{{}_{0}\widehat{2s}_{\,1}}\mathrm{B}_{{}_{1}\widehat{2s}_{\,0}}
onto
\mathrm{B}_{0}\langle 1\rangle
, which is unique up to a
non-zero scalar, does not induce a morphism of complexes
\mathrm{B}_{{}_{0}\widehat{2s}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}^{-s,s}\to\mathrm{B}_{0}\langle 1\rangle
, so the embedding
f^{-s,s}
does not split.

This shows that
\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,0}}\mathrm{Y}\langle t\rangle
and
\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{m}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}
are not isomorphic for any
k,m\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}
such that
k>0
and any
t\in\mathbb{Z}
, which was the last case we had to prove. ∎

Let
\left[\mathbf{U}\right]_{\oplus}
be the split Grothendieck group of
\mathbf{U}
. Since
[\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}]_{\oplus}\cong\widehat{H}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
, the free

\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}]
-module
\left[\mathbf{U}\right]_{\oplus}
carries the structure of an
\widehat{H}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
-module.

Corollary 5.23
.

The
\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}]
-linear map
\gamma_{U}\colon U\to\left[\mathbf{U}\right]_{\oplus}
, defined by

\gamma_{U}(u_{k}):=\left[\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}\right]\quad\text{and}\quad\gamma_{U}(u^{\prime}_{k}):=\left[\mathrm{B}_{\rho}\mathrm{B}_{\widehat{k}_{\,1}}\mathrm{Y}\right],\quad k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0},

is an isomorphism of
\widehat{H}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
-modules.

Proof.

This corollary is an immediate consequence of
Proposition 5.4
and
5.22
.
∎

5.3.2.
A triangulated
\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
birepresentation
\mathbf{W}

Unfortunately, there is no obvious triangulated structure on the category
\mathrm{mod}_{K^{b}(\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext},\diamond}_{2})}(\mathrm{Y})
, e.g., there is no obvious way to define the cone of a morphism between two objects in that category. This is a well-known problem for categories of
modules over algebra objects in triangulated monoidal categories, see e.g.
[
Bal
]
. We will therefore use a different strategy to obtain a triangulated birepresentation
\mathbf{W}
.

This strategy is motivated by the observation that horizontal composition on the right with
\mathrm{Y}^{r,s}
, for
(r,s)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2}
, defines a
\mathbb{Z}^{2}
-action on
K^{b}(\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2})
. To be precise, this is a strong but not a strict action, because
\mathrm{Y}^{r,s}\mathrm{Y}^{r^{\prime},s^{\prime}}
is isomorphic to
\mathrm{Y}^{r+r^{\prime},s+s^{\prime}}
but not equal, in general. The non-trivial isomorphism is given by
\zeta
, defined in
Section 4.2.2
, and the
\mathbb{Z}^{2}
-action is strong precisely because
\zeta

is natural in both entries and satisfies the hexagon identities.

Using this action, we can define the
orbit category

\widehat{\mathbf{\Omega}}:=K^{b}(\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2})/\mathrm{Y}^{\mathbb{Z},\mathbb{Z}}
, which has the same objects as
K^{b}(\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2})
and its morphism spaces are defined by

\mathrm{hom}_{\widehat{\mathbf{\Omega}}}(\mathrm{A},\mathrm{B}):=\bigoplus_{(r,s)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2}}\mathrm{hom}_{K^{b}(\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2})}(\mathrm{A},\mathrm{B}\mathrm{Y}^{r,s}),

for
\mathrm{A},\mathrm{B}\in K^{b}(\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2})
. Composition is defined as in (
136
). By construction, the left regular
K^{b}(\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2})
action on
K^{b}(\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2})
induces a
left
K^{b}(\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2})
-action on
\widehat{\mathbf{\Omega}}
. The natural functor
\Pi_{\widehat{\mathbf{\Omega}}}\colon K^{b}(\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2})\to\widehat{\mathbf{\Omega}}
, which is the identity on objects and sends any morphism

f\colon\mathrm{A}\to\mathrm{B}
in
K^{b}(\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2})
to

f\colon\mathrm{A}\to\mathrm{B}\mathrm{Y}^{0,0}
in
\widehat{\mathbf{\Omega}}
, is a morphism of wide finitary
\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
-bireprentations. In the following proposition, we do not consider any triangulated structures yet.

Proposition 5.24
.

There is an equivalence of wide finitary
\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
birepresentations

\mathrm{add}\left\{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{Y}\colon\mathrm{A}\in K^{b}(\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2})\right\}\cong\widehat{\mathbf{\Omega}},

where the additive closure on the left-hand side is taken in
K^{b}(\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext},\diamond}_{2})
.

Proof.

This is exactly the content of the free forgetful adjunction in (
135
) and
(
136
).
∎

Corollary 5.25
.

The equivalence in
Proposition 5.24
restricts to an equivalence of wide finitary

\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
birepresentations

\mathbf{U}\cong\widehat{\mathbf{\Omega}}^{\prime},

where
\widehat{\mathbf{\Omega}}^{\prime}
is the full
\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
subbirepresentation of
\widehat{\mathbf{\Omega}}
whose objects are those of
\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
, which can be identified with the complexes in
K^{b}(\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2})
concentrated in homological degree zero via the usual embedding.

In order to construct a triangulated
\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
birepresentation, we proceed in two steps. We consider the
\mathbb{Z}^{2}
-action on
K^{b}(\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2})
as generated by
\mathrm{Y}^{1,1}\cong\mathrm{B}_{\rho}^{2}
and
\mathrm{Y}^{0,1}\cong\mathrm{T}_{1}^{-1}\mathrm{B}_{\rho}
. Instead of considering all orbits, we first use results of
[
Eli2
, Section 3.4]
to construct a new wide finitary category
\overline{\mathcal{S}}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
which already contains a canonical isomorphism
\mathrm{B}_{\rho}^{2}\cong R
, and then apply
[
FKQ
, Theorem/Definition 1.1]
to construct a triangulated orbit category from
K^{b}(\overline{\mathcal{S}}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2})
under the action of the second generator.

Recall from (
127
) and
Proposition 5.5
that
W
is isomorphic to the quotient of
\widehat{H}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
by the left ideal generated by

\rho^{2}-1\quad\text{and}\quad\rho-T_{1}.

The first generator is central, so the ideal it generates is two-sided and

(149)

\overline{H}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2}:=\widehat{H}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}/\langle\rho^{2}-1\rangle

is a quotient algebra. Of course, we have

(150)

W\cong\overline{H}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2}/\overline{H}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2}(\rho-T_{1}),

where
\overline{H}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2}(\rho-T_{1})
is the left
\overline{H}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
ideal generated by
\rho-T_{1}
. Elias
[
Eli2
, Section 3.4]
showed that
\overline{H}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
can be categorified by equipping
\widehat{\mathcal{BS}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
with an additional morphism and its ”inverse”, imposing some additional relations,
and defining the new wide finitary monoidal category
\overline{\mathcal{S}}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
as the Karoubi envelope of the additive envelope of this ”enhanced”
\widehat{\mathcal{BS}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
. Concretely, we add the generators

(151)

0
0

and the relations

By
[
Eli2
, Lemma 3.25 and Theorem 3.28]
, there is an isomorphism
\mathrm{B}_{\rho}^{2}\cong R

in
\overline{\mathcal{S}}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
, the split Grothendieck group of
\overline{\mathcal{S}}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
is isomorphic
to
\overline{H}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
and the natural functor
E\colon\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}\to\overline{\mathcal{S}}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
induces the projection
\widehat{H}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}\cong[\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}]_{\oplus}\to\overline{H}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2}\cong[\overline{\mathcal{S}}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2}]_{\oplus}
.

Since
\mathrm{Y}^{1,1}=\mathrm{B}_{\rho}^{2}
, the above implies that
\mathrm{Y}^{r,s}\cong\mathrm{Y}^{0,s-r}
in
K^{b}(\overline{\mathcal{S}}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2})
, for any
(r,s)\in\mathbb{Z}^{2}
. Hence, it suffices to consider a
\mathbb{Z}
-action on
K^{b}(\overline{\mathcal{S}}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2})
, with
s\in\mathbb{Z}
acting by horizontal composition on the right with
\mathrm{Y}^{0,s}=(\mathrm{T}_{1}^{-1}\mathrm{B}_{\rho})^{s}
. Let
\overline{\mathbf{\Omega}}:=K^{b}(\overline{\mathcal{S}}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2})/\mathrm{Y}^{0,\mathbb{Z}}
be the corresponding orbit category and let
\overline{\mathbf{\Omega}^{\prime}}
be its full
\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
subbirepresentation whose objects are those of
\overline{\mathcal{S}}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
, which can be identified with the objects in
K^{b}(\overline{\mathcal{S}}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2})
concentrated in homological degree zero.

Lemma 5.27
.

The natural
\mathbb{R}
-linear monoidal functor
E\colon K^{b}(\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2})\to K^{b}(\overline{\mathcal{S}}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2})

induces a morphism of
\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
-birepresentations
E_{\Omega}\colon\widehat{\mathbf{\Omega}}\to\overline{\mathbf{\Omega}}
, which restricts and corestricts to a morphism of

\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
-birepresentations
E_{\Omega^{\prime}}\colon\widehat{\mathbf{\Omega}}^{\prime}\to\overline{\mathbf{\Omega}^{\prime}}
.

Proof.

On objects, the functor
E_{\Omega}
is defined by the identity map, of course. Given a morphism
f\colon\mathrm{A}\to\mathrm{B}
in
\widehat{\mathbf{\Omega}}
with only one
non-zero component
f^{r,s}\colon\mathrm{A}\to\mathrm{B}\mathrm{Y}^{r,s}
in
K^{b}(\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2})
, for some
r,s\in\mathbb{Z}
, define
E_{\Omega}(f)
as the morphism in
\overline{\mathbf{\Omega}}
whose only one non-zero component
E_{\Omega}(f)^{0,s-r}
is given by postcomposing
E(f)
with the isomorphism
\mathrm{Y}^{r,s}\cong\mathrm{Y}^{0,s-r}
in
K^{b}(\overline{\mathcal{S}}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2})
. This definition can be extended to all morphisms in
\mathrm{hom}_{\widehat{\mathbf{\Omega}}}(\mathrm{A},\mathrm{B})
by additivity.

The definition implies immediately that
E_{\Omega}
is
\mathbb{R}
-linear and sends identity morphisms to identity morphisms, and the hexagon identities and binaturality of
\zeta
guarantee that it also preserves composition. Finally, it is a morphism of left
\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
birepresentations because the isomorphisms
\mathrm{Y}^{r,s}\cong\mathrm{Y}^{0,s-r}
in the definition of
E_{\Omega}
are applied to the rightmost factor of the objects.

The last claim of the lemma follows immediately.
∎

The following result is an immediate consequence of
5.25
and
Lemma 5.27
.

Corollary 5.28
.

The functor
E_{\Omega^{\prime}}
induces a morphism of
\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
birepresentations
E_{\Omega^{\prime}}\colon\mathbf{U}\to\overline{\mathbf{\Omega}^{\prime}}
(for which we use the same notation).

We do not know whether
E_{\Omega^{\prime}}
is an equivalence. It is certainly essentially surjective, because it is the identity on objects, but it is unclear whether it is fully faithful.

The above fits exactly the conditions of
[
FKQ
, Theorem/Definition 1.1]
: the triangulated category
\mathcal{T}:=K^{b}(\overline{\mathcal{S}}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2})
is naturally endowed with the dg-enhancement
\mathcal{A}:=C^{b}_{dg}(\overline{\mathcal{S}}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2})
(the dg-category of bounded complexes in
\overline{\mathcal{S}}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
), and the complex
F:=\mathrm{Y}^{0,1}=\mathrm{T}_{1}\mathrm{B}_{\rho}
naturally yields a dg-bimodule such that the induced endofunctor

H^{0}(F)
on
H^{0}(\mathcal{A})\cong K^{b}(\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2})
is an equivalence (with inverse induced by
\mathrm{Y}^{0,-1}
). This means that there is a canonical triangulated orbit category
\mathbf{W}
of
K^{b}(\overline{\mathcal{S}}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2})
under the action of
\mathrm{Y}^{0,1}
, which in the
notation of
[
FKQ
, Theorem/Definition 1.1]
is defined by

\mathbf{W}:=H^{0}\left(\mathrm{pretr}\left(C^{b}_{dg}(\overline{\mathcal{S}}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2})/\mathrm{Y}^{0,\mathbb{Z}}\right)\right).

The left
\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
-action clearly commutes with the right action by
\mathrm{Y}^{0,1}
, hence

\mathbf{W}
is a triangulated left
\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
-birepresentation.

By
[
FKQ
, Theorem 3.17]
, there is a natural dg-functor

(155)

Q\colon C^{b}_{dg}\left(\overline{\mathcal{S}}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2}\right)\to\mathrm{pretr}\left(C^{b}_{dg}\left(\overline{\mathcal{S}}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2}\right)/\mathrm{Y}^{0,\mathbb{Z}}\right),

which induces a triangle functor
Q^{\triangle}:=H^{0}(Q)
between the homotopy categories

(156)

Q^{\triangle}\colon K^{b}\left(\overline{\mathcal{S}}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2}\right)\to\mathbf{W}.

As
Q^{\triangle}
is a morphism of triangulated
\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
-birepresentations, it induces a morphism of
[\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}]_{\oplus}
-modules between the triangulated Grothendieck groups

(157)

\left[Q^{\triangle}\right]_{\triangle}\colon\left[K^{b}\left(\overline{\mathcal{S}}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2}\right)\right]_{\triangle}\to\left[\mathbf{W}\right]_{\triangle}.

A well-known general result on Grothendieck groups, see e.g.
[
Ro
]
, implies
that
[K^{b}(\overline{\mathcal{S}}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2})]_{\triangle}\cong[\overline{\mathcal{S}}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}]_{\oplus}\cong\overline{H}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
. Thus (
157
) yields a morphism of
\widehat{H}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
-modules

q\colon\overline{H}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2}\to\left[\mathbf{W}\right]_{\triangle}.

We claim that this morphism in an epimorphism. Indeed, consider the dg functor Q in (35). The objects of
C^{b}_{dg}(\overline{\mathcal{S}}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2})/Y^{0,\mathbb{Z}}

are the same as those of
C^{b}_{dg}(\overline{\mathcal{S}}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2})
. In taking the pretriangulated closure, we add cones, but those do not generate new elements in the Grothendieck group, proving the claim.

By construction, horizontal composition with
\mathrm{Y}^{0,1}
is naturally isomorphic to the identity functor on

\mathbf{W}
, so
q
factors through
W
by (
150
), resulting in a commutative triangle

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\overline{H}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces W}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\left[\mathbf{W}\right]_{\triangle}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces q}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\gamma_{W}}

Surjectivity of
q
implies surjectivity of
\gamma_{W}
. Recall also that
W^{\mathbb{C}(q)}
is simple, see
Proposition 5.2
. However, we do not know that
\left[\mathbf{W}\right]_{\triangle}^{\mathbb{C}(q)}
is non-zero, which is why we have to
settle for a conjecture.

Conjecture 5.29
.

The morphism

\gamma_{W}^{\mathbb{C}(q)}\colon W^{\mathbb{C}(q)}\to\left[\mathbf{W}\right]_{\triangle}^{\mathbb{C}(q)}

is an isomorphism.

Finally, recall the morphism of
\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
birepresentations
E_{\Omega^{\prime}}\colon\mathbf{U}\to\overline{\mathbf{\Omega}^{\prime}}
from
5.28
. By
[
FKQ
, Remark 3.12]
, there is an equivalence of wide finitary
\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
birepresentations

\overline{\mathbf{\Omega}}\cong H^{0}(C^{b}_{dg}(\overline{\mathcal{S}}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2})/Y^{0,\mathbb{Z}}).

Precomposition with
E_{\Omega^{\prime}}
and postcomposition with the canonical functor
H^{0}(C^{b}_{dg}(\overline{\mathcal{S}}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2})/Y^{0,\mathbb{Z}})\to H^{0}(\mathrm{pretr}(C^{b}_{dg}(\overline{\mathcal{S}}^{\,\mathrm{ext}}_{2})/Y^{0,\mathbb{Z}}))
yields
a morphism of
\widehat{\mathcal{S}}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{2}
birepresentations

(158)

\Pi^{\mathbf{U}}_{\mathbf{W}}\colon\mathbf{U}\to\mathbf{W}.

We conjecture that
\Pi^{\mathbf{U}}_{\mathbf{W}}
categorifies the projection
\pi^{U}_{W}
in

Proposition 5.5
, meaning that the following diagram commutes

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces U}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces W}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\left[\mathbf{U}\right]_{\oplus}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\left[\mathbf{W}\right]_{\oplus}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\left[\mathbf{W}\right]_{\triangle}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\gamma_{U}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi^{U}_{W}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\gamma_{W}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\left[\Pi^{\mathbf{U}}_{\mathbf{W}}\right]}
